text: Zik laughed softly.
speaker: Narrator

text: The sound surprised all three of them.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu tilted her head.
speaker: Narrator

text: First laugh in three days.
speaker: Enhedu

text: I wasn't keeping count.
speaker: Zik

text: I was.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Balag looked from one to the other.
speaker: Narrator

text: I preferred it when neither of you talked.
speaker: Balag

text: You've said that before.
speaker: Enhedu

text: I'll say it again.
speaker: Balag

text: Enhedu rested a hand on the repaired section of wall.
speaker: Narrator

text: It'll fail.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Eventually.
speaker: Zik

text: You know that.
speaker: Enhedu

text: Everything fails.
speaker: Zik

text: So why fix it?
speaker: Enhedu

text: Zik tightened the final knot.
speaker: Narrator

text: Because failure doesn't mean today.
speaker: Zik

text: The three of them stood looking at the wall for another moment.
speaker: Narrator

text: The repair wasn't invisible.
speaker: Narrator

text: It wasn't meant to be.
speaker: Narrator

text: The new cord crossed the old brick in pale lines that anyone could see.
speaker: Narrator

text: Someone else would come along one day and know another pair of hands had cared enough to keep it standing a little longer.
speaker: Narrator

text: That was all. He finished the last knot, tested the repaired section with his weight, and stood. The wall still leaned a little. It no longer looked like it was giving up.
speaker: Narrator

text: Enhedu had wandered over during the work. She crouched, picked up one of the loose bricks Zik had set aside, weighed it in her hand, then set it neatly back into the gap he hadn't needed. No comment. Just the brick returned to where it belonged.
speaker: Narrator

text: They didn't rest long after that. The light was already sliding toward the kind of copper dusk that made distances hard to trust. Zik adjusted a slipped pack strap on the nearer donkey while the others drank. The motion was automatic. His hands knew the work even when his mind was somewhere else.
speaker: Narrator

text: Balag watched him a moment longer than necessary.
speaker: Narrator

text: You still thinking about the Collector?
speaker: Balag

text: I'm thinking about what I'm not going to tell him.
speaker: Zik

text: Balag gave a short nod, as if that answer was the only one he'd expected.
speaker: Narrator

text: They started walking again. The broken ground gradually gave way to the first real tracks—cart ruts, donkey dung, the scuffed places where people had stood arguing about tolls or water or nothing important at all. The smell of the city grew stronger. Smoke. Onions. The particular sourness of too many bodies living too close together.
speaker: Narrator

text: Zik felt the mark under the linen give a single slow pulse. Not a demand. Just a reminder that it was still there.
speaker: Narrator

text: He kept walking.
speaker: Narrator

text: Ahead, the first low roofs of the outer districts hunched against the darkening sky.
speaker: Narrator
